**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Agreement contains no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant of any kind. I checked:

- **Text searches** for "solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "recruit" — no hiring restriction surfaced.
- **§ 14 (Miscellaneous)** — assignment, waiver, governing law/arbitration, notices, independent contractors, severability, force majeure, subcontracting, bankruptcy, integration. No restrictive covenant.
- **§ 10 (Confidentiality)** — a single sentence limiting use of Confidential Information under the separate NDA; no personnel restriction.
- **§ 13 (Shared Resources)** — the section most likely to carry one, given Commerce One operations, consulting and engineering personnel work alongside Corio personnel. It addresses only Employee NDA/Invention Agreements and ownership of Developments.
- **Exhibit D, § 5 (Personnel)** — each party assigns one sales/marketing employee; no hiring restriction.
- **§ 14.10** integration clause confirms nothing outside the Agreement, Exhibits, NDA and SOW imposes such a covenant.

This sits at the **preferred position** — no non-solicit binding us as Customer — rather than the fallback, so there is nothing to narrow and no redline is appropriate. The absence operates in our favour: Corio remains free to hire Commerce One personnel, including the operations, consulting and engineering staff embedded with Corio teams under § 13.

One drafting note for awareness rather than action: because § 13 contemplates Commerce One personnel working alongside Corio personnel, Commerce One may raise a non-solicit at signature or in the concurrent NDA or Statement of Work (both incorporated by reference under § 14.10, and neither reviewed here). If it does, our fallback is a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and no no-hire.
